newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong in epidemic alert, launches measles jabs.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong in epidemic alert, launches measles jabs.

text.p: Hong Kong authorities have issued a measles alert and launched a drive to immunise more than one million children to prevent an epidemic.
The campaign will target those aged one to 19, health authorities said. More than 2,000 people have been hit by a current outbreak this year, and a 16-year-old boy recently died from complications.

"To prevent a major outbreak from occurring in a crowded community like Hong Kong, it is necessary for the immunity of the community to reach a level of about 94 percent," deputy director of health Paul Saw said on Tuesday night.

Studies showed the immunity of those aged one to 19 was less than 86 percent. Some children had received single-dose immunisation but should have a second dose to boost immunity. The immunisation drive will start next month.
Measles gives sufferers a pinkish rash and is highly contagious and untreatable. The last epidemic in Hong Kong was in 1988, when 3,162 people were hit and eight died.
